title: Propagation latency mitigation and ops cheat notes
content:
Notes to self: propagation latency across caches/edge nodes is the hidden cause of most ‘weird’ deploy incidents. This is a scattershot brain-dump + lightweight playbook for next time we do a regional model flip or multi-tier rollout. Intention: make a reproducible checklist and experiment plan that I can run with SRE/QA before any big flip.

Background and symptoms I've seen:
- After a model flip, some clients continue hitting the old model (stale pinned metadata, SDK caches) for up to N minutes, causing semantic drift in production requests.
- Proxy/edge config propagation (nginx reloads, envoy xDS) can be near-instant in one region and delayed in another due to control-plane rate-limiting.
- Token/tenant-level routing (per-tenant routing table) takes longer to converge when combined with client-side SDK caches and sticky sessions.

Hypotheses:
1) Client SDK caches (30s–5m default) + server-side prefix caches create a two-stage consistency window.
2) Control-plane push failures correlate with bursts of rollout traffic (autoscaler churn).
3) The majority of user-facing errors we see after flips are from session-affinity mismatch rather than model logic regressions.

Quick definitions for this doc:
- propagation latency: time between making a routing/variant change and >99% traffic seeing that change
- soft-handshake: short-lived mechanism to accept both old and new model responses until client confirms new model behavior

Immediate pre-rollout experiments (run on canary cluster):
- Measure baseline convergence: flip a dummy feature flag and record percent of traffic seeing new value over time (sample at 1s, 5s, 15s, 30s, 60s, 120s).
- Client SDK test harness: spawn 500 simulated clients with realistic cache TTLs and sticky cookies; flip routing and measure skew.
- Control-plane throttle test: issue 50 rapid config updates across 10 regions to surface rate-limits.

Observability queries to run (examples):
- percent_new = sum(rate(requests{version=\"new\"}[1m])) / sum(rate(requests[1m])) by (region)
- median_prop_time = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(config_propagation_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
- session_mismatch_rate = increase(session_affinity_mismatch_total[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m])

Practical rollout steps (staged):
1) Preflight (30–120m before): announce window, turn on verbose tracing for canary cohort, reduce SDK cache TTL to 10s for internal test clients.
2) Warmup (0–10%): route a small internal cohort + shadow 10% of canary to see responses. Collect semantic diffs for top-100 prompts.
3) Soft-handshake phase: accept both old/new variants for a short client-token grace period; set a handshake cookie on success. This lets long-lived sessions transition naturally.
4) Observe convergence; if propagation latency > expected threshold, hold and investigate control plane errors or CDN purge backlog.
5) Increment traffic in cautious steps (10 -> 25 -> 50 -> 75 -> 100) with 10–30m observation windows depending on latency profile.

Escape hatches and thresholds:
- Immediate rollback if model error rate jumps > 3x baseline for two consecutive windows.
- If session_mismatch_rate > 1% and persists beyond 15m, revert routing and escalate to SRE.
- If median_prop_time in any critical region > 60s, pause increases and run control-plane diagnostics.

Tactical commands / quick checks:
- Check propagation logs: kubectl -n controlplane logs -l app=config-pusher --since=15m | grep \"push.*failed\"
- Force some nodes to refresh xDS: curl -X POST http://node-ops/refresh-xds -d '{\"region\":\"us-west2\"}' (internal endpoint)
- Purge CDN prefix for model metadata: aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id ABCD --paths \"/model-metadata/*\"

Client-side mitigation ideas:
- SDK: expose a short-lived forced-refresh API to re-evaluate routing when the client sees a ”model mismatch” error.
- Add jittered TTL decay: clients reduce cache TTL gradually during a rollout window to avoid mass-refresh storms.

Telemetry and postmortem notes to capture:
- time_to_50pct and time_to_95pct propagation per region, per rollout direction (up / down)
- list of clients that observed mixed-model sessions (trace id list)
- control-plane error traces and queue lengths during rollout windows

Experiment backlog (tickets to cut):
- Add synthetic canaries that exercise long-lived session handoffs (ticket: JIRA-PI-4871).
- Implement SDK forced-refresh endpoint and document usage patterns.
- Build a small dashboard that shows propagation curves per region vs. historical baseline.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to collaborate on):
- What is the right handshake cookie TTL? (30s vs 300s vs session length)
- Should we adopt an explicit two-phase routing commit (prepare/commit) for high-risk flips? Tradeoffs: latency vs complexity.
- How to surface slow-propagation risk automatically in the Console (red/yellow flags on rollout panel)?

Hand-off checklist for SRE on-call when doing a propagation-sensitive flip:
- Confirm control-plane push quotas and recent error rates.
- Verify CDN invalidations for model metadata are queued and OK.
- Keep a quick rollback command handy and notify the database/metrics team for rapid access to traces.

Paper trail / short script for runbook snippet:
- rollout_start() { 
    echo \"Starting %TARGET% rollout\"; 
    gh pr comment $PR --body \"starting canary rollout\"; 
    kubectl apply -f routing-change.yaml
  }
- rollback() { 
    echo \"Rolling back to previous routing\"; 
    kubectl apply -f routing-previous.yaml; 
    alert #sre on slack \"rolled back: $RUN_ID\";
  }

Personal follow-ups:
- Run the client SDK harness tomorrow with 1k clients and 3 TTL profiles.
- Pair with Omar to instrument session_mismatch counter to include tenant id.
- Draft a Console feature mock that highlights slow-propagation risk on rollout UI.

Random scribbles / heuristics:
- If you see >5 distinct models observed in a single tenant session trace, that session is probably broken.
- Favor soft-handshake + small windows over big instantaneous flips when in doubt.
- Run propagation measurement every Friday after deploys to keep baseline fresh.

---
End of notes. This is a living scratchpad; add more concrete experiments and flip scripts as we validate.
